newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-Big Australia bank mergers said no problem.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-Big Australia bank mergers said no problem.

text.p: The managing director of Westpac Banking Corp, Bob Joss, said on Tuesday he had no philosophical problem with mergers between Australia's four major banks.

"We have to be more convenient and reach customers in more ways but not through the old fashioned store mechanism which is a very high cost way - if a merger can do that and competition can be strong and intense then I would see no philosophical reason for anybody to be opposed to mergers," Joss said at a media briefing after Westpac announced annual results.
Joss said Australia's major banks' non-interests costs were too high and the challenge for banks was to reduce these costs.

"We have to find ways to be more efficient and that means perhaps fewer but larger branches so the cost per customer or cost per desposit is lower and means more alternative channels like telephones or ATMs (Automatic Teller Machines)," Joss said.

The Australian government is currently reviewing financial market regulation, which has until now barred mergers between the big four banks. These include Westpac, Australia and New Zealand Banking Group Ltd, National Australia Bank Ltd and the Commonwealth Bank of Australia.
The inquiry into financial regulation, which is expected to release a discussion paper next month, is headed by businessman Stan Wallis.
The inquiry will look at the regulatory framework governing banking, superannuation and other financial institutions.
